summary.en: President Murmu addressed the Bastar Dussehra festival in Chhattisgarh, indicating a shift from Maoist violence toward development. The Kuki-Zo Women’s forum called for President's Rule in Manipur, describing the crisis as political rather than security related. Bastar is reported to be leaving the Maoist shadow and stepping into growth. IndiGo extended flight cancellations to Saudi Arabia because of security concerns. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: President Murmu holdt en tale på Bastar Dussehra-festivalen i Chhattisgarh, og indikerte et skifte fra maoistisk vold til utvikling. Kuki-Zo-kvinnesamfunnet krevde presidentstyre i Manipur, og beskrev krisen som politisk snarere enn sikkerhetsrelatert. Det rapporteres at Bastar forlater den maoistiske skyggen og går inn i vekst. IndiGo utvidet kanselleringene av fly til Saudi-Arabia på grunn av sikkerhetsbekymringer. 437 dødsfall i kamp ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
